description:
## Why this issue exists

Stoa-mail allows users to set passwords with no minimum length or complexity requirements. NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1 requires: ≥8 characters minimum (15 for privileged accounts), no mandatory complexity rules, and optionally checking against known-breached password lists.

## What needs to be done

- Add password validation at the password-change and account-creation endpoints in stoa-mail.
- Enforce minimum length: 8 characters for regular users, 15 for admin/privileged accounts.
- Do NOT enforce complexity rules (NIST explicitly discourages them as they reduce entropy without improving security).
- Optionally: integrate HIBP (Have I Been Pwned) k-anonymity API to reject passwords found in breach corpora. Gate behind a config flag (enabled by default in production mode).
- Return a clear error message on rejection: `400 Bad Request` with `description: "Password must be at least 8 characters"`.
- Write tests: 7-char password rejected, 8-char accepted, known-breached password rejected (if HIBP enabled).

## Acceptance criteria

- Passwords shorter than 8 chars rejected at change/create endpoints
- Admin account creation requires ≥15 chars
- Error message does not reveal implementation details beyond length requirement
- HIBP check is config-gated and off by default (to avoid external dependency in CI)

## Design notes

Regulatory refs: NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.1. No bcrypt/argon2 changes needed — this is purely input validation before hashing. bcrypt max input length (72 bytes) is a separate consideration; document the truncation behaviour.
title: Password policy: minimum length and breach check
